scenes.title: Open Analytics and read the reporting scope

captions.text: In Core, open the Records navigation and choose Analytics.
The selected Executive summary tab gives the department's recorded summary.
Start with From, To, Station slash group and Definition.
This example displays August second through October thirty-first,
with All station groups and All definitions selected.
Read the Generated line and Records read count with those filters.
The page says that dashboards are computed on demand over finalized
Records, and that viewers see the Records they are authorized to open.
Your account's access and the displayed reporting scope both
matter when comparing results.

scenes.title: Read headline figures with the prior period

captions.text: Scroll to Headline figures and read the prior-period
dates before comparing values.
Here, Records finalized is four, Personnel hours and Training hours are each zero
point five, and Amendments is one.
Incident reports, unit responses and the NERIS counts are zero
in this fictional dataset.
The values beneath the tiles show their comparison with the prior period.
These are measures derived from the saved software records.
They do not independently confirm physical attendance, service delivery or a
department's real operational performance.

scenes.title: Distinguish lifecycle, queue and breakdown measures

captions.text: Continue to Lifecycle, Queues and obligations, By month and By definition.
Median hours to finalize is zero point one here, while several
unavailable measures show a dash.
A dash is not a measured zero.
Open drafts shows one and Awaiting review shows zero.
Those are current visible-queue counts, rather than the finalized-record
count of a selected definition.
The breakdown tables show four October records, split between
two Training records and two community software-exercise records.
Use the headings, counts, hours and shares together to understand
what each panel is describing.
Return to the filter row and select Training in Definition.
Before you choose Filter, the earlier Generated line
still says Records read, four.
This separates a prepared field selection from refreshed dashboard output.
Check the intended dates and group at the same time, then choose
Filter to request the new result.
Selecting a reporting filter changes the question you ask of
the saved data; it does not edit, finalize or delete a record.
After choosing Filter, read the returned filter row and generated result.
Training remains selected, and Records read is now two.
The dates and All station groups remain the same.
This readback establishes which definition subset the dashboard actually loaded.
When comparing two views, verify their returned selections and counts
before attributing a difference to changing activity in your department.
Scroll to the refreshed headline figures.
Records finalized is now two, while Training hours and Personnel
hours remain zero point five.
The broader four-record view included two community exercise records with
no recorded hours, so narrowing to Training changes the count
without changing these hour totals.
Amendments remains one.
Compare each named measure with its own purpose rather than assuming every tile
must change when a filter is applied.

scenes.title: Apply a station or group filter

captions.text: Return to Station slash group, select Engine fifty-one and choose
Filter, keeping Training selected.
The returned page says Records read, zero.
Read that zero with the selected group, definition, dates
and your account's access.
It describes this saved Records subset.
It does not establish that the whole department has no activity, that nobody
attended training, or that records outside your authorized view do not exist.

scenes.title: Keep record and transition scopes distinct

captions.text: In this filtered result, Records finalized and Training hours are zero,
while Amendments still shows one.
For this department-administrator account, that amendment figure counts
department transitions in the time window; it is not the finalized-record
count of the selected group.
The empty breakdown panels say No finalized Records in this window.

scenes.title: Restore and verify the broader scope

captions.text: Select All station groups and All definitions, then choose Filter again.
The returned Generated line reads four records.
This restores the broader reporting scope without changing the saved records.
Recheck these selections whenever you move between a narrowly scoped
question and a department-wide review.
A useful comparison begins with a deliberate, verified scope.

scenes.title: Open Workload and recheck its filters

captions.text: Choose the Workload tab for another view of the same recorded activity.
Recheck its date, group and definition filters and the Generated count.
Here, it reads four records, with zero point five Record hours,
Personnel hours and Training hours.
These headings describe different measures even when their
displayed values happen to match.
Use this view to understand how recorded work is distributed, while
checking the underlying entries when a result needs explanation.

scenes.title: Read workload counts, hours and shares

captions.text: Scroll to By month and By definition.
October contains four records and zero point five hours.
In the definition table, Training has two records, zero point five
hours and a fifty-percent share.
The community software-exercise definition also has two records and a fifty-percent
share, but zero recorded hours.
Equal record counts do not mean equal recorded duration.
Read all three columns before deciding where more detail or a
closer records review is needed.

scenes.title: Compare timing, participation, authors and groups

captions.text: Continue to Records by weekday and hour, then the person, unit,
author and station-group panels.
The matrix distributes these recorded entries by their timestamps.
By person shows Matthew Casey with one entry and zero point five hours.
By author shows Wallace Boden with four records.
By station group separates Command from Firehouse fifty-one.
Participation, authorship and group assignment answer different questions.
The unit panel has no finalized Records in this window.

scenes.title: Use a clear reporting question for your department

captions.text: Start with a reporting question that matches your department's records.
Community paramedicine and mental health teams can review outreach
documentation, search-and-rescue teams can compare mission-support
records, security companies can examine recorded service activity, and
wildland or industrial response teams can review their own documented work.
Fire and EMS departments can use the same filter and readback habits.
Choose the intended window, definition and group, refresh the view, then investigate
the underlying records before drawing conclusions from a count or hour total.
